dataset_family: BioFIND (MEG+MRI; MRC Cognition & Brain Sciences Unit Cambridge and Centre for Biomedical Technology Madrid), accessed via DPUK
method_family: Resting-state sensor-space MEG spectral power/covariance (Morlet wavelets, Riemannian), with a FreeSurfer hippocampus/total-grey-matter ratio as the volumetric comparator (electrophysiology)
what_it_shows: Gaubert et al. (2025), eBioMedicine 114:105659. 117 BioFIND MCI patients: 64 progressed to AD dementia and 53 stayed stable; the MRI subset is n=104. In-sample logistic regression: Model 2 (age, education, MMSE, hippocampal ratio) AUC 0.75; Model 3 (the same clinical variables plus posterior 16-38 Hz MEG power) AUC 0.81; Model 4 (both) AUC 0.84. AIC was 132.6, 118.6 and 113.4 respectively. The bootstrap CI for the AUC difference between Model 4 and Model 2 was 0.026-0.179. In Model 4, MEG power (AME -0.12, p < 0.001) and the hippocampal ratio (AME -0.11, p = 0.005) were both independent predictors. Cross-validated stacking: MEG covariance AUC 0.74, MRI cortical volumes 0.77, all inputs 0.81.
why: Identity: the PDF's title, authors (Gaubert, Garces, Hipp, Bruna, Lopez, Maestu, Vaghari, Henson, Paquet, Engemann) and DOI 10.1016/j.ebiom.2025.105659 match the block and the map. I read the whole extract to the References. STATED = partly, on the basis round 20 applied to P-478 and P-581. The study shows a functional measure predicting MCI-to-AD conversion and adding significantly to hippocampal volume. But volume was NOT preserved or non-discriminative: the hippocampal ratio was itself an independent, significant predictor, and in the cross-validated model MRI cortical volumes were the best single brain input (0.77 vs 0.74 for MEG covariance). 'Late' is not tested. NARROWED = yes. The study itself runs the head-to-head, and the non-volumetric measure carried information beyond hippocampal volume: adding MEG to the hippocampal model improved discrimination (CI 0.026-0.179), and MEG plus clinical variables beat hippocampus plus clinical variables on AUC and AIC. Volume stayed discriminative, which matches the narrowed wording's closing sentence. Caveats, from the paper itself: (1) The logistic-regression AUCs are in-sample. (2) The MEG cluster was chosen after exploring the data (the authors' own 'risk of circularity'). (3) Site is collinear with progression (23/27 progressors at CBU vs 41/90 at CTB). The site-adjusted spectral difference was not significant after cluster correction, though the additive contribution of MEG and the hippocampal ratio survived adding site to Model 4. (4) AD diagnosis was clinical, without CSF or PET; the authors estimate about 30% misdiagnosis risk. (5) Follow-up duration is not documented per patient. (6) Progressors had lower baseline MMSE, which the models adjust for. Independence: BioFIND is distinct from every current supporter dataset. No authors are shared with P-584 (Gallego-Rudolf, Wiesman, Yakoub, Zetterberg, Blennow, Baillet, Villeneuve) or any other supporter. But the METHOD family (resting-state MEG spectral power) is the same as P-584's MEG alpha power, so under H.1 it adds no distinct method family unless the operator splits MEG families. P-577 is the registry duplicate stub of this paper (duplicate_of P-488, the same 117 participants) and must not be counted separately. Not a preprint. In the quotes, ligatures, line-break hyphens, curly apostrophes and minus signs are normalised to ASCII.

quotes.quote: In logistic regression models, decreased MEG 16-38Hz spectral power and reduced hippocampal volume/total grey matter ratio on MRI were independently linked to higher AD progression risk.

Model 2 combining age, education, MMSE and hippocampus/total grey matter ratio had a 0.75 AUC (95% CI: 0.67-0.85), a sensitivity of 72% and a specificity of 72%. Then, we created a model that combined clinical and demographic variables with MEG to explore the added value of electrophysiology to clinical information: Model 3 combining age, education, MMSE and cluster MEG power better explained the data than Model 1 and 2, with an AUC of 0.81 (95% CI: 0.74-0.90)

In contrast, the comparison between Model 2 and Model 4 showed a much clearer, significant difference, with a confidence interval from 0.026 to 0.179, highlighting a substantial improvement in Model 4's discrimination capacity over Model 2 that only used MRI.
Model 4, with an AIC of 113.4, had best trade-off between fit and complexity, followed by Model 3 (AIC: 118.6), Model 2 (AIC: 132.6), and Model 1 (AIC: 136.9).
For both, MEG, and MRI the reduction of progression risk was on the order of 10% (AME = -0.12, z = -5.75, p < 0.001 and AME = -0.11, z = -2.83, p = 0.005, respectively)

controlling for multiple comparisons with cluster-permutation testing and keeping the previous detection thresholds, we found no statistically significant differences between groups after adjustment on site.

It can be seen that despite the pronounced and expected site effect (given the strong imbalance of progression rates), the significantly additive contribution of MEG and hippocampal ratio to explaining progression risk was preserved.
The best marginal performance was observed for MEG covariances (AUC = 0.74, SD = 0.13) and MRI cortical volumes (AUC = 0.77, SD = 0.14).
It also increased the risk of circularity as our choice of the MEG power was based on visual-statistical exploration.
